Measured on current main rather than assumed. lifePlaceStateIdentities() returns 52 identities and US-PR is one of them, so the game already seats Puerto Rico as a jurisdiction. What it does not have: no legislature rule pack (only nine exist, for AK IL KY MD MN MO NE NV OH), no candidate-qualification rows, and place-county-relations explicitly excludes Puerto Rico from its summary-level 155 source, so the place-to-county membership that ordinary town queries rely on is absent there.

The D.C. precedent is the model to follow, not a template to copy: D.C. has an approved separate scope in this project and a council rather than a legislature, so the answer should say where Puerto Rico is like D.C. and where it is not.

This matters more than a coverage number because absence of a rule pack currently reads as PERMISSION in this engine rather than as unknown. A player in an uncovered jurisdiction can be offered an office nobody checked they qualify for.
Spanish is the working language of much of the primary source. Official Spanish-language citations are expected and fine; say which language each source was read in.
question: What does Puerto Rico's government actually consist of, for a game that now seats it as a jurisdiction? Specifically: which offices a person can hold and how each is filled; the Legislative Assembly's two chambers, their sizes, term lengths and the at-large and district seats; the qualification rules for each seat — minimum age, residence in Puerto Rico and in the district, and how long each is required, with the assessment moment; the Governor's term and qualification; the Resident Commissioner's term, which is not the same length as a House term; and at local level, what the 78 municipios are, how a mayor and a municipal legislature are chosen, and what powers a municipio actually has. Separately: do Puerto Rico's municipios appear in the Census source that produces the national local-government count, and if so as what class?

title: What Puerto Rico's government is, now that it is in scope
usableAnswer: Enough to author a rule pack and qualification rows the way the nine existing states have them: per office, the term length, how the seat is filled, and the qualification fields with their units and the moment each is assessed, each with an official citation. For the municipios, the count, what a municipal government consists of, how its mayor and legislature are chosen, and which powers are genuinely municipal rather than commonwealth. For the census question, a yes or no with the class name and the source table, so the local-government count can either include them or say why it does not. Where a rule genuinely has no counterpart in a state, say so plainly rather than mapping it onto the nearest state concept.
whyItMatters: The game seats Puerto Rico today and knows nothing about it, and in this engine that is worse than not seating it: a missing rule pack currently reads as permission rather than as unknown, which is how a twenty-one-year-old was once offered a governorship. Every coverage number the project has published says 'fifty states and D.C.', so the arithmetic in the briefs, the candidacy work and the research summaries is all one jurisdiction short and nobody has checked whether the offices it does generate there are coherent. It also decides whether the national range — the generated fallback used where no researched pack exists — is a defensible instrument for a place whose institutions are not a state's, which is the open half of a separate question.

answer.summary: Governor: four-year term from January 2, no term limit; 35 or older with five years' U.S. citizenship plus Puerto Rico citizenship and residence, tested at the election. Legislative Assembly: 27 senators (8 districts of 2 plus 11 at-large) and 51 representatives (40 districts plus 11 at-large); art. III s7 minority seats can raise these counts; members 30 or older (Senate) or 25 (House), two years in Puerto Rico and one in the district, tested at the election; terms start January 2 and the four-year length is derived, not stated; a veto override needs two-thirds. Resident Commissioner: four-year term from January 3 (48 U.S.C. 891), 25 or older and able to read and write English (s892). 78 municipios: the mayor is 21 or older with one year's domicile, tested at taking office, starting the second Monday of January; municipal legislatures have 16, 14 or 12 seats by population (San Juan 17, Culebra 5), members 18 or older with six months' domicile before filing (Ley 107-2020, March 11, 2026 consolidation). The Census counts municipios in the county-government class. Voters: Electoral Code s5.3.
